candidate_politicians.name: 김도연
roles: Minister of Finance (1949 central-bank reform request)
candidate_politicians.evidence: Bank of Korea archive states the June 1949 adviser request was sent in Finance Minister Kim Do-yeon's name.

candidate_politicians.name: 최순주
roles: Chair, Bank of Korea Establishment Committee
candidate_politicians.evidence: Bank of Korea archive identifies Finance Minister Choi Sun-ju as chair of the establishment committee created under Presidential Decree No.350.
candidate_politicians.open_lead: Extract committee appointment list and meeting minutes to distinguish chair authority from collective decisions.

candidate_politicians.name: 구용서
roles: Vice-chair, Bank of Korea Establishment Committee
later Minister of Commerce and Industry

candidate_politicians.name: 전진한
event_links: Korean Confederation of Labor factional conflict

candidate_politicians.open_lead: Open the December 1952 National Assembly stenographic record and extract motion wording, co-sponsors, vote and subsequent committee referral.

candidate_politicians.name: 박술음
candidate_politicians.evidence: AKS biography links his ministerial tenure to Trade Union Act and Labor Standards Act social legislation.
candidate_politicians.open_lead: Verify exact ministerial tenure and ministry bill-submission role from gazettes, cabinet minutes and National Assembly bill records; do not infer personal authorship from tenure.

candidate_politicians.name: 백두진
candidate_politicians.evidence: Retained from Pass 260; this pass adds Bank of Korea wartime institutional context but no new personnel-grade primary record.
candidate_politicians.open_lead: Locate 1953 emergency monetary-measure cabinet and Finance Ministry records.

adversarial_checks: Test whether central-bank independence was a Korean-government design claim or primarily imported adviser language; preserve both drafting and adoption layers.
Test whether Kim Do-yeon's request for advisers implies authorship of the final Bank of Korea Act; it does not without committee and Assembly records.
Test whether Choi Sun-ju's committee chairmanship implies unilateral control; committee decision rule required majority support.
Test whether Gu Yong-seo's first-governor role makes him author of the law; distinguish design, establishment and operation.
Test whether democratic wording of 1953 labor laws maps to actual enforcement under Rhee; union-control evidence points to a separate implementation question.
Test whether Jeon Jin-han's priority motion equals sole authorship of the labor-law package; identify co-sponsors, committees and amendments.
Test Park Sul-eum biography claims against ministry and Assembly primary records before assigning proposed_by.
Test claims that 1952 local elections were simply a presidential constitutional tactic against statutory implementation history and local actor evidence.
Test party-strength narratives using candidate/elected counts while separating city councils from town/village/provincial results.
Test retrospective BOK institutional narrative against contemporaneous cabinet, Assembly and ECA/Federal Reserve records.
